sb_prompt: SEE HOW THE OTHER CALLER FEELS ABOUT THE PROPOSAL THAT ALL YOUNG AMERICANS SHOULD SPEND A YEAR OR TWO DOING SOME KIND OF PUBLIC SERVICE
raw_output:
ParticipantA: Hello!
ParticipantB: Hi there. You got the wrong number?
ParticipantA: No, I did the right number. Just wanted to chat about that proposal.
ParticipantB: Oh, the service thing? Yeah, I got that too.
ParticipantA: Right. So, I'm gonna be honest, I'm a little skeptical about it myself.
ParticipantB: Me too. Honestly, I'm pretty on the fence about it.
ParticipantA: Yeah. I mean, I'm a manager at a grocery store, and it feels like we're already stretched pretty thin.
ParticipantB: Yeah, I drive a school bus. That's just one of those jobs that's kind of all-consuming.
ParticipantA: I know. It's just, I don't know, I've held onto this doubt for a while now.
ParticipantB: Same here. It's been sitting in the back of my head for years.
ParticipantA: Exactly. I can't really articulate why, but it just doesn't feel right.
ParticipantB: I get that. I feel like my own kids are already doing enough without forcing it.
ParticipantA: That's fair. My kids are older now, and they're figuring things out on their own.
ParticipantB: Yeah, kind of like that. Sometimes you wonder if it's just another layer of bureaucracy.
ParticipantA: Exactly. It feels a bit like solving a problem we didn't necessarily create.
ParticipantB: True. Like, who decided it's better for everyone to do this?
ParticipantA: I guess that's the hard part. The "who" is missing.
ParticipantB: Yeah. I don't think anyone really listened to people like us, doing the day-to-day.
ParticipantA: No, that's it. I feel like the people doing the actual work are the ones who'd know best.
ParticipantB: Amen to that. I think we're done here?
ParticipantA: Yeah, I think so. Thanks for talking.
ParticipantB: Yeah, thanks. Good talking to you.
ParticipantA: Bye.
ParticipantB: Bye.
